content.prompt: In a survey of 450 people, 38% preferred coffee, 42% preferred tea, and the rest preferred neither. How many people preferred neither?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage preferring neither}&=100\%-38\%-42\%\\\text{Percentage preferring neither}&=20\%\\\text{Number preferring neither}&=20\%\times450\\\text{Number preferring neither}&=0.20\times450\\\text{Number preferring neither}&=90\end{align*}$$
90 people preferred neither.

classification.difficultyReason: Move from a numerical comparison to a general explanation by representing both percentage expressions algebraically and using commutativity of multiplication.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Which is greater: $15\%$ of $80$ or $80\%$ of $15$?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}15\%\text{ of }80&=15\%\times80\\15\%\text{ of }80&=0.15\times80\\15\%\text{ of }80&=12\\80\%\text{ of }15&=80\%\times15\\80\%\text{ of }15&=0.80\times15\\80\%\text{ of }15&=12\end{align*}$$
They are equal.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why $x\%$ of $y$ will also be equal to $y\%$ of $x$.

answer.short: They are equal because both are $\dfrac{xy}{100}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x\%\text{ of }y&=\frac{x}{100}\times y\\x\%\text{ of }y&=\frac{xy}{100}\\y\%\text{ of }x&=\frac{y}{100}\times x\\y\%\text{ of }x&=\frac{xy}{100}\end{align*}$$
So, they are equal.

content.prompt: Donald says, ‘prices have gone down by 500%’. Explain why this is impossible.

inlines.text: times the original. This gives a negative price, which is impossible for an ordinary sale price.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage remaining}&=100\%-500\%\\&=-400\%\\\text{Decrease multiplier}&=-400\div100\\&=-4\end{align*}$$
The new price would be $-4$ times the original positive price, so it would be negative. An ordinary sale price cannot be negative; the greatest possible decrease is 100%, leaving a price of zero.

content.prompt: In a survey, 35% of respondents said they felt a penalty was too lenient and 20% felt it was too harsh. If there were 1200 respondents, how many felt the penalty was appropriate?

answer.worked:
The percentage who felt the penalty was appropriate is $100\%-35\%-20\%=45\%$.

$$\begin{align*}10\%\text{ of }1200&=1200\div10=120\\5\%\text{ of }1200&=120\div2=60\\45\%\text{ of }1200&=4\times120+60\\&=540\end{align*}$$

540 respondents felt the penalty was appropriate.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}50\%\text{ of }30&=30\div2=15\\10\%\text{ of }30&=30\div10=3\\60\%\text{ of }30&=15+3=18\end{align*}$$

Eric must score more than 18 marks to improve on 60%, so the least whole-number score is 19 marks.

children.label: a
children.prompt: “To find $30\%$ of $50$, I multiplied by $1.3$ and got $65$”

answer.short: She increased $50$ by $30\%$ instead of finding $30\%$ of $50$. Use $0.3$; the correct answer is $15$.
answer.worked:
The multiplier $1.3$ increases an amount by $30\%$. Finding $30\%$ requires the multiplier $0.3$.
$$\begin{align*}30\%\text{ of }50 &= 0.3\times50\\&=15\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: “To increase $80$ by $25\%$, I multiplied by $0.25$ and got $20$”

answer.short: She found $25\%$ of $80$ instead of increasing it by $25\%$. Use $1.25$; the correct answer is $100$.
answer.worked:
The multiplier $0.25$ finds only the extra amount. The original must also be retained.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Required percentage} &= 100\%+25\%\\&=125\%\\\text{New amount} &=1.25\times80\\&=100\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: “To decrease $120$ by $40\%$, I multiplied by $0.4$ and got $48$”

answer.short: She found $40\%$ of $120$ instead of decreasing it by $40\%$. Use $0.6$; the correct answer is $72$.
answer.worked:
The multiplier $0.4$ finds the amount removed. The remaining amount is $60\%$ of the original.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Remaining percentage} &=100\%-40\%\\&=60\%\\\text{New amount} &=0.6\times120\\&=72\end{align*}$$

Offer A gives a 10% discount on both boxes. Offer B charges full price for one box and half price for the other.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Offer A total} &= 2\times\text{£}5\times0.90\\\text{Offer A total} &= \text{£}9.00\\\text{Offer B total} &= \text{£}5.50+\text{£}5.50\times0.50\\\text{Offer B total} &= \text{£}8.25\\\text{Difference} &= \text{£}9.00-\text{£}8.25\\\text{Difference} &= \text{£}0.75\end{align*}$$
Option B is the better deal by £0.75.

The negative result means a $22.\dot{2}\%$ decrease.

inlines.text: Which made the higher percentage profit?

answer.short: A: $30\%$ profit; B: $25\%$ profit. Investment A made the higher percentage profit.
answer.worked:
Investment A:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Profit} &= \$650-\$500\\&=\$150\\\text{Percentage profit} &= \frac{150}{500}\times100\%\\&=30\%\end{align*}$$
Investment B:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Profit} &= \$1000-\$800\\&=\$200\\\text{Percentage profit} &= \frac{200}{800}\times100\%\\&=25\%\end{align*}$$
Investment A made the higher percentage profit because $30\%>25\%$.

content.prompt:
An elephant calf weighed 115 kg when born. The calf grew to an adult weighing 5.93 tonnes.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Final mass}&=5.93\times1000\text{ kg}\\\text{Final mass}&=5930\text{ kg}\\\text{Change in mass}&=5930-115\\\text{Change in mass}&=5815\text{ kg}\\\text{Percentage change}&=\frac{5815}{115}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage change}&\approx5057\%\end{align*}$$
The positive change represents an increase.

content.prompt:
Emma completed a worksheet in 2:18 (minutes:seconds).
A week later, she completed the same worksheet in 1:45.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original time}&=(2\times60+18)\text{ s}\\\text{Original time}&=138\text{ s}\\\text{Final time}&=(1\times60+45)\text{ s}\\\text{Final time}&=105\text{ s}\\\text{Percentage change}&=\frac{105-138}{138}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage change}&\approx-23.9\%\end{align*}$$
The time decreased by $23.9\%$.

content.prompt: Chloe is running a tuck shop. She buys a pack of 12 chocolate bars for $\$3.50$. Give percentage answers to 2 decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Chloe sells all the chocolate bars for 60c each. Work out her percentage profit.

answer.short: $105.71\%$ profit. Total sales are $\$7.20$; profit is $\$3.70$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total selling price}&=12\times\$0.60\\\text{Total selling price}&=\$7.20\\\text{Profit}&=\$7.20-\$3.50\\\text{Profit}&=\$3.70\\\text{Percentage profit}&=\frac{3.70}{3.50}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage profit}&\approx105.71\%\end{align*}$$
The percentage profit is $105.71\%$ to 2 decimal places.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Work out Chloe's percentage profit if she sells one third of the chocolate bars for 60c each and the rest for 30c each.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bars sold for 60c}&=\frac13\times12\\\text{Bars sold for 60c}&=4\\\text{Bars sold for 30c}&=12-4\\\text{Bars sold for 30c}&=8\\\text{Total selling price}&=4\times\$0.60+8\times\$0.30\\\text{Total selling price}&=\$4.80\\\text{Profit}&=\$4.80-\$3.50\\\text{Profit}&=\$1.30\\\text{Percentage profit}&=\frac{1.30}{3.50}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage profit}&\approx37.14\%\end{align*}$$
The percentage profit is $37.14\%$ to 2 decimal places.
